# 

# 1\. LAB OVERVIEW

## 1.1  Why This Lab Exists

Dynatrace is one of the most widely used enterprise observability platforms. Its strengths are automatic discovery (OneAgent), a live dependency model of everything it monitors (Smartscape), end-to-end distributed traces (PurePath), an AI engine that groups related anomalies into one problem with a root cause (Davis), and a data lakehouse (Grail) that you query with DQL. Operations engineers mostly use it to answer "is it broken, what is affected, and why" — in that order.  
In this lab you log in with your browser to a pre-configured shared Dynatrace SaaS Grail tenant. An Ubuntu EC2 host (ip-172-30-0-220) runs the easyTravel application (frontend → backend → database) and is already instrumented with OneAgent, so there is nothing to install or type. You inspect the host and its Smartscape topology, follow a failed request through a PurePath, triage the Davis AI problem card, and finish in a Notebook where three DQL queries line up the deployment, the error logs and the p95 latency.

| 🎯  NIIT iRUN Alignment |
| :---- |
| INCIDENT OWNERSHIP: You can open any Dynatrace problem card and explain impact, affected entities, root cause and the visual resolution path. |
|  |
| TROUBLESHOOTING EXCELLENCE: You will move from host to topology, from a failed PurePath to the exception and service ID, and from the problem card back to the affected service without losing context. |
|  |
| OPERATIONAL READINESS: You can duplicate a Notebook and run time-bounded DQL queries to correlate a deployment with errors and latency — safely, on a shared tenant. |

## 1.3  Conceptual Foundation

Dynatrace builds one model of your environment and attaches every signal to it. Learn the names of the parts first.  
*Figure: Dynatrace Building Blocks — OneAgent → Grail (Logs, Spans, Metrics, Events, Entities) → Smartscape Topology → Davis AI → Problems → Apps (Infrastructure & Operations, Services, Distributed Tracing, Notebooks)*

| Concept | What It Is | Where to Find It | In This Lab |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Hosts / processes / services | Monitored entities with IDs (HOST-…, PROCESS\_GROUP-…, SERVICE-…) | Infrastructure & Operations, Services apps | Host ip-172-30-0-220; easyTravel frontend, backend, database |
| Smartscape | Live dependency graph: horizontal (calls) and vertical (host → process → service) | Smartscape app / entity pages | frontend → backend → database |
| PurePath (distributed trace) | One request end to end with all spans | Distributed Traces app | Failed checkout (HTTP 500\) with CreditCardCheckError500 |
| Davis AI / problems / Grail | AI that correlates anomalies into problem cards; Grail stores all data for DQL | Problems app; Notebooks | easyTravel problem card; 3 DQL queries |

*Figure: Problem Card Anatomy in Dynatrace — Title & Category · Status (Active/Closed) · Impact · Affected Entities · Root Cause (Davis) · Visual Resolution Path · Events Timeline*

* Log in to a shared Dynatrace Grail tenant and find the monitored easyTravel host

# 3\. CONCEPT DEEP-DIVE BEFORE STARTING

## 3.1  How Data Gets Into Dynatrace — and What You See in This Lab

OneAgent is installed on the host and automatically discovers the host, its processes and (for supported technologies such as Java) deep code-level traces. OpenTelemetry is the vendor-neutral alternative, where applications or a Collector send traces, logs and metrics over OTLP. In this lab everything comes from OneAgent on the EC2 host ip-172-30-0-220: easyTravel is a Java application, so OneAgent captures its services, PurePaths, logs and the deployment event automatically. All of it lands in Grail and on the same Smartscape. You only read it — the platform is already set up for you.

| 💡  Why This Matters Operationally |
| :---- |
| Davis does not send you fifty alerts for one outage — it opens one problem, lists every affected entity, and points to the most likely root cause. |
|  |
| Every Dynatrace entity has an ID (HOST-…, SERVICE-…). Using IDs in DQL and tickets avoids confusion when names repeat across environments. |

## 3.2  The Critical Distinction: Problem vs Event vs Alert

An event is a single detected anomaly or change (CPU saturation on a host, a deployment such as CUSTOM\_DEPLOYMENT, a failure rate increase on a service). Davis correlates related events into one problem — the card you work on — and alerting profiles decide which problems notify people. You therefore triage problems, read events for evidence, and compare event timestamps with errors and latency.

| ⚠️  Most Common Mistake When Starting with Dynatrace |
| :---- |
| A new user searches the Problems list, sees a card already Closed or does not see one at all, and concludes "Dynatrace did not detect it" or "nothing is happening". |
|  |
| REASON: The timeframe was too short, or the fault window had already ended, so the problem is Closed and only visible with a wider timeframe. |
|  |
| YOU MUST set the timeframe to "Last 2 hours" and look at both Active and Closed problems before drawing conclusions. |

## 3.3  Where Things Live in Dynatrace

| Question | App / View | Entity / Data | DQL Starting Point |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Is the host healthy? | Infrastructure & Operations → Hosts | HOST ip-172-30-...., processes | timeseries avg(dt.host.cpu.usage), from: now() \- 2h |
| Which services exist and how do they perform? | Services | SERVICE (easyTravel frontend, backend, database) | timeseries percentile(dt.service.request.response\_time, 95), from: now() \- 2h |
| Where did one request fail? | Distributed Traces (PurePath) | Spans and exceptions of one trace | fetch spans, from: now() \- 2h \| filter trace.id \== … |
| What is broken and why? | Problems | dt.davis.problems | fetch dt.davis.problems, from: now() \- 2h |

| 📝  How to Decide Where to Start in Dynatrace |
| :---- |
| Ask: "Is there an open problem?" If yes, start from the problem card — it already lists the affected entities and root cause. If no, start from the affected service (Services) or host (Infrastructure & Operations), then open traces and logs from there. Use DQL in a Notebook for a custom view — and always bound it with a time filter. |

Grail stores every signal in one place. You open the instructor's template Notebook, click Duplicate so that you work on your own copy, rename it Lab1-\<YourName\>, and run three pre-built DQL queries — each bounded to the last 2 hours — to line up the error logs, the deployment event and the p95 latency on one timeline.

| ⌨  Task 4 — Notebooks (Ctrl/Cmd+K → "Notebooks" → open the template → Duplicate) |
| :---- |
|  |
| \# Step 1 (UI): Open \[TEMPLATE\] 30-Min Observability Lab → click Duplicate → rename the copy Lab1-\<YourName\> |
| \#   Work only in your copy. Never edit the template. Run each section with Run (or Ctrl/Cmd+Enter). |
|  |
| \# Query 1 (Error Logs) |
| fetch logs |
| \| filter timestamp \> now() \- 2h |
| \| filter status \== "ERROR" or matchesPhrase(content, "Exception") |
| \| fields timestamp, dt.entity.service, dt.entity.host, status, content |
| \| limit 20 |
|  ![][image1]  |
| \# Query 2 (Deployment Events) |
| fetch events |
| \| filter timestamp \> now() \- 2h |
| \| filter event.kind \== "DAVIS\_EVENT" or event.type \== "CUSTOM\_DEPLOYMENT" |
| \| fields timestamp, event.type, event.name, dt.entity.service |
| \| limit 20 |
| ![][image2] |
| \# Query 3 (p95 Latency Line Chart) — set the visualization to Line chart |
| timeseries p95 \= percentile(dt.service.request.response\_time, 95), by: { dt.entity.service }, from: now() \- 2h |
| **📟  Expected Output** |
| Query 1: error log lines mentioning the credit card check / HTTP 500, with SERVICE-… and HOST-… entity IDs (HOST \= ip-172-30-0-220) |
| Query 2: a CUSTOM\_DEPLOYMENT event named "easyTravel Checkout Service v2.4.1 Rollout" with its timestamp |
| Query 3: p95 lines per service; the backend line rises after the deployment timestamp (response time is in microseconds) |

# 6\. TROUBLESHOOTING — COMMON ISSUES & FIXES

| Issue / Error | Cause | Diagnosis | Fix |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Login fails or "access denied" | Not in group Cohort-40, wrong tenant URL, or an expired session | Open the URL again in a private window; check the user menu | Use the URL from your lab admin; ask the instructor to confirm Cohort-40 |
| Host or services not listed | Timeframe too short or wrong tenant | Check the timeframe selector and the tenant ID in the URL | Set Last 2 hours; search ip-172-30-0-220 or easyTravel |
| No failed traces / no problem visible | Fault window ended or filters too narrow | Remove filters; set Last 2 hours; include Closed problems | Tell the instructor to re-run Appendix A (fault \+ deployment event) |
| Duplicate is missing or the Notebook will not save | You opened the template from a shared view, or lack personal write permission | Check the Notebooks list; look for the ⋮ menu → Duplicate | Ask the instructor; never edit the template |
| DQL: no records / unknown field / permission denied | No data in the window, field names differ, or the query lacks storage read permission | Run: fetch logs, from: now() \- 2h \| limit 5 and inspect the fields | Adjust field names to your records; report permission errors to the instructor |
| Query is slow or times out | 40 learners run queries at once, or no time filter | Confirm from: now() \- 2h in the query | Wait 30 seconds and run once; do not click Run repeatedly |

# 7\. INSTRUCTOR DEBRIEF — 3 MINUTES

## 7.1  Discussion Questions (pick two if time is short)

| Discussion 1 — Host to Service to Trace |
| :---- |
| Starting from host ip-172-30-0-220, how did you reach the failing service? |
| What does OneAgent give you without any setup on the application? |
|  |
| Key answer to explore: host → process → service → PurePath; OneAgent discovers all of it automatically for supported runtimes such as Java. |
| **Discussion 2 — Smartscape in an Incident** |
| How does the vertical Smartscape help when a host has a problem? |
| How does the horizontal view (frontend → backend → database) help when a service fails? |
|  |
| Key insight: vertical shows what runs on the host; horizontal shows who calls whom — the blast radius. |
| **Discussion 3 — Davis Problem Cards** |
| Which fields of the problem card pointed you to the backend service? |
| Why does one problem with a root cause beat many alerts? |
|  |
| Key answer: impact, affected entities, root cause and resolution path; fewer, correlated notifications reduce noise. |
| **Discussion 4 — Deployment, Logs and Latency in Grail** |
| What did the three DQL queries show about the v2.4.1 rollout and the errors? |
| Why is a time filter mandatory on a shared tenant? |
|  |
| Answer: errors and p95 start after the deployment timestamp; time filters protect shared query capacity and keep results fast. |

## 7.2  Common Mistakes — Learn From These

| Mistake | Why It Happens | Consequence | Prevention |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Running DQL with no time filter | Habit from other tools | Slow query, load on a shared tenant | Always add from: now() \- 2h |
| Editing the template Notebook | Skipping Duplicate | Other learners lose the template | Duplicate first, rename Lab1-\<YourName\> |
| Reading only the top of a problem card | Title looks sufficient | Wrong service investigated | Read impact, affected entities, root cause and resolution path |
| Ignoring entity IDs | Names look unique | Wrong entity compared across Tasks 2–4 | Record HOST-… and SERVICE-… IDs |
| Closing or commenting on a shared problem | Curiosity | Spoils the exercise for the other learners | Read only; never press Close, Mute or Add comment |

# APPENDIX A — INSTRUCTOR PRE-CLASS RUNBOOK (5 MINUTES BEFORE COHORT)

Instructor only. The runbook takes about 5 minutes; start it 15 minutes before class on the EC2 host ip-172-30-0-220. Learners never see or run these commands.

| ⌨  Appendix A — Instructor pre-class runbook (run on EC2 ip-172-30-0-220, 15 minutes before class) |
| :---- |
|  |
| \# Step 0: Variables. DT\_API\_TOKEN is an API token with the events.ingest scope. Use the live URL (qcw66226.live.dynatrace.com), not .apps |
| export DT\_ENV\_URL="https\://qcw66226.live.dynatrace.com" |
| export DT\_API\_TOKEN="\<api-token-with-events.ingest\>" |
| export FAULT\_MINUTES=10 |
|  |
| \# Step 1: Post the CUSTOM\_DEPLOYMENT event (the rollout marker used in Task 4 Query 2\) |
| curl \-sS \-X POST "\$DT\_ENV\_URL/api/v2/events/ingest" \\ |
|   \-H "Authorization: Api-Token \$DT\_API\_TOKEN" \-H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \\ |
|   \-d '{"eventType":"CUSTOM\_DEPLOYMENT","title":"easyTravel Checkout Service v2.4.1 Rollout","entitySelector":"type(HOST),entityName.equals(\\"ip-172-30-0-220\\")","properties":{"deployment.name":"easyTravel Checkout Service v2.4.1 Rollout","deployment.version":"v2.4.1","source":"instructor-runbook"}}' |
|  |
| \# Step 2: Enable the CreditCardCheckError500 fault plugin on the easyTravel backend |
| curl \-s "http\://localhost:8091/services/ConfigurationService/setPluginEnabled?name=CreditCardCheckError500\&enabled=true" |
|  |
| \# Step 3: Switch the plugin off again after FAULT\_MINUTES (runs in the background) |
| (sleep \$((FAULT\_MINUTES\*60)); curl \-s "http\://localhost:8091/services/ConfigurationService/setPluginEnabled?name=CreditCardCheckError500\&enabled=false") & |
| **📟  Expected Output** |
| JSON response with "reportCount":1 and status OK (HTTP 200\) |
| HTTP 200 / 204; within 3–8 minutes HTTP 500 traces and a Davis problem appear in the tenant |
| After 10 minutes the plugin is off; the problem closes a few minutes later |

| ⚠️  INSTRUCTOR ONLY — Notes for 40 Concurrent Learners |
| :---- |
| Verify before class: group Cohort-40 (storage:\*:read plus personal Notebook write) contains all learners; the template \[TEMPLATE\] 30-Min Observability Lab exists and runs; at least one failed PurePath and one problem are visible. |
|  |
| If the problem should still be Active during class, set FAULT\_MINUTES to 40 and, if it closes early, run Steps 1–3 again. Remind learners that a Closed problem is fine and that every DQL query needs from: now() \- 2h. |
